newsitem.title: UK: LCH to introduce interest rate swap, FRA clearing.
newsitem.headline: LCH to introduce interest rate swap, FRA clearing.

text.p: The London Clearing House (LCH) said on Wednesday it had agreed in principle to introduce a facility for clearing interest rate swaps and Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs) traded on the OTC interbank market.
It said in a statement it would implement swaps clearing in the first half of 1999.

LCH was planning to clear "plain vanilla" interest rate swaps and FRAs in major currencies -- dollar, mark, yen, sterling, French franc, lira and euro when introduced -- for maturities out to 10 years. There would be no standardisation of dates, it said.
"Swaps players are telling us that the time is now right for the introduction of a clearing facility for interbank swaps," said Chief Executive David Hardy.
Feasibility studies during the past five months had revealed that most swap players were interested in LCH clearing swaps.
LCH said the main advantages would be freeing up of credit lines, significant operational savings through fewer payments, more efficient use of collateral and reduction in operational risk.
There would also be margin offsets with LIFFE (London International Financial Futures Exchange) business, and reduced capital requirements.
LIFFE's Chief Executive Daniel Hodson supported LCH's decision.
"Margin offsets with OTC products will be another major reason to choose to trade short term interest rate and bond contracts on LIFFE," Hodson said.
LCH said the next stage of the project was to confirm the detailed operational and contractual requirement for swaps clearing.

LCH acts as a counterparty for trades executed by its members on LIFFE (incorporating London Commodity Exchange), the London Metal Exchange (LME), the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) and Tradepoint.
